Week 1: October 9 to October 18, 2026. 25 current Reel formats people are copying right now, each explained in plain words with ways to use it for your business. Pick the ones that fit; your This Week list says how many to film. Borrow the format and the text idea, and bring your own footage, buyer, and next step. We can't give you rights to any song: when the audio note says to swap it, swap it.
1This is your signReach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 25) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: Grab 5 to 8 seconds of everyday footage of your product, workspace, or finished result.

On-screen text: "This is your sign to [the thing you sell or fix]." End on one line with your next step.

For your business:

  • Handyman: a sagging gate + "This is your sign to finally fix the gate. Free quotes, link in bio."
  • Etsy tees: a folded tee on a Sunday table + "This is your sign to own one shirt that's just for doing nothing."
  • Photographer: golden-hour light in a field + "This is your sign to book the fall photos before the leaves drop."
Open this audio in Instagram

No special audio: use your own voice, the natural sound of the work, or a cleared track.

2Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy…Reach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (SocialPilot report, Sept 10 to 24, 2026) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: One clip of your product or result, shown plainly, 5 to 8 seconds.

On-screen text: "Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy [your product or result]." Keep it light and specific.

For your business:

  • Bakery: a box of cookies opening + "…but it can buy a dozen brown-butter cookies."
  • Digital kit: an invite being edited in Canva + "…but it can buy a party invite you finished in 10 minutes."
  • Consultant: a clean project board + "…but it can buy a week without missed deadlines."

3"Some people call me…"Reach + Sell

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 11) · about 5 minutes to make

Film: Two or three quick clips of you at work, one per line.

On-screen text: List what people usually call you ("Some people call me the fence guy. Some call me Frank."), then land on "But you can call me when [the problem you solve]."

For your business:

  • Handyman: "…but you can call me when the fence starts leaning."
  • Photographer: "…but you can call me when you want photos your kids actually smile in."
  • Etsy shop: "…but you can call me when you need a gift by Friday."

4The processTrust + Reach

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 18) · about 10 minutes to make

Film: Four or five 1-second clips: your tools or materials, two steps of the work, then the finished result.

On-screen text: One line on the first clip: "How [product] gets made" or "What a [service] actually involves." Optional short labels per step.

For your business:

  • Print-on-demand: design on screen, mockup, package, finished tee on a hanger.
  • Handyman: old post, digging, concrete, straight fence.
  • Digital kit: blank template, edit name, change colors, finished invite.

5Once a day, once a week, once a monthTrust

Trending on Instagram Reels (Later's weekly tracker, Sept 25) · about 10 minutes to make

Film: Three short clips, one for each bucket.

On-screen text: "Once a day: [x]. Once a week: [y]. Once a month: [z]." Use the habits of your work or of your customer.

For your business:

  • Handyman: "Once a day: answer quotes. Once a week: check my own gutters. Once a month: sharpen everything."
  • Etsy shop: "Once a day: pack orders. Once a week: new design. Once a month: restock the bestseller."
  • Consultant: "Once a day: clear the inbox. Once a week: client check-ins. Once a month: audit my own workflow."

No special audio: use your own voice, the natural sound of the work, or a cleared track.

8Deadpan stare + "me after…"Reach

Spreading on TikTok among small accounts (newest use we saw: Sept 20; 11 creators, 9 small accounts). Not yet confirmed on Instagram: tap the sound on Instagram before you use it · about 1 to 2 minutes to make

Film: A few seconds of you at work, looking flatly at the camera.

On-screen text: "Me after [the Nth time something predictable happens]." One line, about your work, never about a real customer.

For your business:

  • Handyman: "Me after the 3rd client this week says it's probably a quick fix."
  • Etsy seller: "Me after someone asks if the $28 shirt comes in 14 more colors."
  • Consultant: "Me when the 1-hour call was booked as a quick 15."

Trend audio: original sound, skidmark3000 (a creator's original sound). If Instagram shows it in the audio picker, you can try it; if not, or if you're unsure, the format works with your own voice or the natural sound.

14Hands over the lens: before → afterReach + Trust

Spreading on TikTok among small accounts (newest use we saw: Sept 23; examples are beauty, business use is our adaptation). Not yet confirmed on Instagram: tap the sound on Instagram before you use it · about 5 minutes plus the "after" to make

Film: Film the "before," push your hands over the lens, then pull them away on the "after" in the same spot.

On-screen text: Optional: "[the fix] in one afternoon."

For your business:

  • Handyman: broken step → hands → fixed step.
  • Market seller: empty table → hands → full display.
  • Organizer: messy shelf → hands → clean shelf.

Trend audio: original sound, xvsuellen (a creator's original sound). If Instagram shows it in the audio picker, you can try it; if not, or if you're unsure, the format works with your own voice or the natural sound.
